title: Random example cost for a low-degree learner
statement: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a rational learning parameter $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$, the random example cost is the cardinality of the family of low-degree Fourier components on $n$ bits with cutoff $k$, multiplied by the number of samples per coefficient for that family and parameter.
